newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - AUG 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - AUG 1.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

-- The Association of Greek Industrialists (SEV) has called the government to introduce bolder economic measures through the 1998 budget to be drafted latyer in coming months. In its monthly bulletin, SEV claims that stabilisation policies have run out of steam and cannot bring about convergence of the Greek economy to European Union norms and reduce unemployment.

-- The European Union (EU) has blocked the award of the Thessaloniki subway project to the Thesaloniki Metro consortium until the legal grounds on which the Greek state rejected a bid by rival Macedonian Metro consortium have been verified by its legal service.

-- Greece is in negotiations with EU officials for the transfer of subsidies totalling 600 billion drachmas into large infrastructure works from projects on agriculture, fishing, and regional development which exhibit low absorption.

-- The finance ministry will resort to foreign borrowing totalling $2.0 billion in September to top up its cash reserves and meet its large fiscal needs which exceed 2.0 trillion drachmas. The new loans will bring Greece's total foreign borrowing in 1997 to its $4.0 billion target.

-- Excess liquidity continues to feed through to inflation, money supply figures for June show. The Bank of Greece's intermediary targets for M3 money supply growth, 6.0-9.0 percent, is grossly overshot with M3 growing 15.4 percent.

-- The ministry of national economy will divert EU funds totalling 400 billion drachmas to Greece's railways and hospitals as part of a reshuffle of EU financial aid between sectors with varying levels of absorption of subsidies.

-- Transparency hinders development in the case of the Public Power Corporation's large power plant slated for construction in Florina. Pressure from a large number of parliament members across the political spectrum who claimed partial treatment of the succesful bidder forced the government to hire an international auditor through a tender to rule whether the accepted bid was the best among those submitted.

-- According to an amendment submited to a bill in the parliament, the government has moved its June 25, 1997 deadline for incorporation of all utilites two years back, to 1999, because it failed to bring about the necessary changes in their legal status.

-- A single negative vote by a syndicalist postponed for coming September a decision by the Board of OTE telecom on the supply of digital lines valued at 83 billion drachmas and other equipment valued at 100 billion, needed for OTE's investment programme.

-- Statistics from Greece's statistics service and development ministry show that Greek consumer price inflation is mostly fueled by hikes in utility rates and excessive rises in the cost of services provided by a large number of trades which took place in the past year or so.
